sections.content:
Population change in Newcastle-under-Lyme in 2032

The population in Newcastle-under-Lyme is projected to increase from 125,404 people in 2022 to 127,922 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in births and deaths, which will decrease the population by 4,248 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Newcastle-under-Lyme
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Newcastle-under-Lyme, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 4,248, with 10,378 births and 14,626 deaths in Newcastle-under-Lyme between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Newcastle-under-Lyme by 3.4%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 4,005, with 92,495 people moving to the area and 88,490 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Newcastle-under-Lyme by 3.2%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 298, with 2,772 people moving to the area and 3,070 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Newcastle-under-Lyme by 0.2%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 3,166, with 6,126 people moving to the area and 2,960 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Newcastle-under-Lyme by 2.5%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Newcastle-under-Lyme in 2032

The median age in Newcastle-under-Lyme is projected to remain the same at 43 years between 2022 and 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 23% of the population in Newcastle-under-Lyme are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 20% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Newcastle-under-Lyme between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Newcastle-under-Lyme is projected to stay the same, at around 63%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 322 to 336 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Newcastle-under-Lyme?

In 2032, 18% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 20% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Newcastle-under-Lyme between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 7% to 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
